title: Neutral stances on hot topics can damage your reputation, study finds
titleZh: 研究发现：保持中立并不讨喜
summary:
人们或许不应畏惧表明自己的真实立场。弗吉尼亚大学的一项最新研究为此提供了证据。在北美地区开展11项相关研究后，研究人员发现，在争议性议题上自称中立的人往往更容易受到质疑。该研究的主要负责人之一、弗吉尼亚大学公共政策、工商管理与心理学副教授加布里埃尔·亚当斯指出：“当一个人表达中立立场时，他人往往会对此抱有强烈怀疑，甚至认为持这种立场的人道德水平更低——基本上，他们被看作与持相反观点者一样不道德。”

来源：phys.org；作者：Jane Kelly；原文发布时间：2026-01-18 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: People shouldn't be afraid to say what they think, and new research from the University of Virginia bears that out. Across 11 studies in North America, researchers found people who claim neutrality on controversial issues are often met with skepticism. "When someone expresses a neutral viewpoint, we are really skeptical of that neutral viewpoint, and we actually think that they are less moral—basically as immoral as someone who holds an opposing viewpoint," said Gabrielle Adams, an associate professor of public policy, business administration and psychology who was among the leaders of the studies.
paragraphs.contentZh: 人们或许不应畏惧表明自己的真实立场。弗吉尼亚大学的一项最新研究为此提供了证据。在北美地区开展11项相关研究后，研究人员发现，在争议性议题上自称中立的人往往更容易受到质疑。该研究的主要负责人之一、弗吉尼亚大学公共政策、工商管理与心理学副教授加布里埃尔·亚当斯指出：“当一个人表达中立立场时，他人往往会对此抱有强烈怀疑，甚至认为持这种立场的人道德水平更低——基本上，他们被看作与持相反观点者一样不道德。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In one of the 11 studies, Adams and her team recruited 600 online participants, asking them to read about a colleague who either supported, opposed or claimed neutrality on increasing immigration. They then asked the participants to rate the colleague's morality. The research team also measured participants' own views on immigration. "Unsurprisingly, targets whose views aligned with the participants were rated more favorably," Adams said. "However, targets who expressed a neutral view were rated just as poorly as targets whose views on that topic were opposed to participants."
paragraphs.contentZh: 在这11项研究中的其中一项，亚当斯及其团队招募了600名线上参与者，请他们阅读关于一位同事的描述，该同事在是否应增加移民的问题上，分别被设定为支持、反对或表示中立三种情况。随后，参与者需对这位同事的道德水平进行评分。同时，研究团队也记录了参与者本人在移民议题上的立场。亚当斯指出：“正如预期，与参与者立场相同的被评价者获得了更高的道德评分。但那些表达中立的人所得到的道德评价，几乎与那些和参与者立场相左的人一样低。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In another study, Adams' team asked 605 people online to imagine sitting down at a holiday dinner and saying something like, "Hey, I heard the neighborhood is debating whether to open a safe drug injection site nearby. What do you all think about it?" The researchers then had them imagine one of the dinner guests responded by saying they were neutral, in favor of or opposed to the site. They also asked participants how they personally felt about the issue. "Overall, participants saw the guest who took a neutral stance as more conflict-avoidant and strategic than someone who agreed or disagreed with them," Adams said. "At the same time, they also viewed the neutral guest as more apathetic and indecisive about the issue compared to guests who clearly took a side."
paragraphs.contentZh: 在另一项研究中，亚当斯的团队邀请了605名线上参与者，请他们想象在一个围坐一桌的节日晚餐中，有人提起：“我听说社区正在讨论是否要在附近设立一个安全的毒品注射点。你们怎么看？”接着，研究人员让参与者设想其中一位宾客回应自己持中立、支持或反对的态度。研究团队同时也询问了参与者本人对该议题的看法。亚当斯总结道：“总体来看，参与者认为在这一问题上保持中立的宾客，相比明确支持或反对的人，更倾向于回避冲突，也显得更有策略性。但与此同时，相比立场鲜明的宾客，中立者也被更多地视为对议题态度冷淡，并且更优柔寡断。”

paragraphs.contentEn: In a third scenario, using a nationally representative sample, the scientists asked participants to imagine scrolling past a social media post where the person posting said they were either against, neutral on or in favor of a controversial issue. As you'd expect, people rated posters who shared their views the most positively. What stood out, though, was that posters who took a neutral position were rated just as negatively as those who openly disagreed with them.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在第三个实验场景中，研究人员选取了一组具有全国代表性的样本，让参与者想象自己在浏览社交媒体时，看到一条帖子，发帖人就某个争议议题表达了反对、中立或支持的立场。结果与预期一致，参与者对观点相同者的评价最为正面。但一个突出的发现是， 那些持中立立场的发帖人，受到的负面评价与公开持反对立场的人一样多。

paragraphs.contentEn: Taken together, the 11 studies brought this conclusion: "People think that this neutrality is essentially a way to play both sides," Adams explained. It's a way to come across as maintaining a strategically favorable reputation and being empathetic and avoiding conflict. The problem is that the way that it actually comes across to other people is that you don't have a backbone.
paragraphs.contentZh: 亚当斯解释说，综合这11项研究，我们得出的结论是：“在很多人看来，这种中立立场实质上是一种两边都不得罪的做法。”人们往往认为，保持中立既能维系对自己有利的策略性声誉，又显得富有同理心，还能避免卷入冲突。 但问题在于，在他人眼中，这种做法恰恰暴露出一个人缺乏主见。

paragraphs.contentEn: "This is a kind of study that suggests that people shouldn't be afraid to say what they think. It might suggest that taking a neutral stance actually isn't the best route to having civil and respectful conversations. The more productive route to a civil conversation would be to say you think and to explain what you think, because misalignment isn't the worst thing in the world." Adams said the study results surprised her. "What we wanted to know with this study is whether neutrality is rewarded or not," she said. "What we think we're trying to achieve by being neutral is not the attribution that others are actually making. I think that's, for me, the big takeaway of this article."
paragraphs.contentZh: 亚当斯指出：“这类研究表明，人们或许不必害怕表达自己的真实看法。研究结果也提示我们，采取中立立场并非促成文明且相互尊重对话的最佳方式。相比之下，更有利于推动对话的做法是清晰陈述自己的观点，并阐明理由，毕竟观点不同本身并不是不可接受。”亚当斯坦言，研究结果让她感到意外。她说：“我们做这项研究是想了解保持中立是否有好处。但现实是，我们自以为通过保持中立想要实现的效果，与他人对我们的实际评价并不一致。我认为，这正是这项研究带来的最大启示。”

expressions.expression: …… is a way to come across as ……. The problem is that the way that it actually comes across to other people is that ……
expressions.meaning: ……旨在营造一种……。但问题在于，在他人眼中，这种行为实际给人的印象却是……。
expressions.example: Micromanaging is often seen as a way to come across as diligent and detail-oriented. The problem is that the way that it actually comes across to employees is that the manager lacks trust in their abilities.
expressions.exampleZh: 微观管理常被视为一种旨在表现出勤勉和注重细节的方式。但问题在于，在员工眼中，这实际给人的印象是管理者对他们的能力缺乏信任。

keySentences.analysis:
写作积累句型
例句：Micromanaging is often seen as a way to come across as diligent and detail-oriented. The problem is that the way that it actually comes across to employees is that the manager lacks trust in their abilities.
翻译：微观管理常被视为一种旨在表现出勤勉和注重细节的方式。但问题在于，在员工眼中，这实际给人的印象是管理者对他们的能力缺乏信任。
